chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Playing a missing arrangement from memory at the dance
summary: On the job he lacked one chart, closed his eyes and played the whole arrangement from memory after one run-through, which he credits to a photographic memory.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No. No, I'm in rehearsal. And that's what I say, I'm playing, I'm knocking out all these tunes, and she say one of these days, if you keep studying, you'll be pretty good. So naturally --

Naturally I'm -- you know, I'm knocked downstairs. She say I'm pretty good. I think I'm pretty good now. What the heck, I'm playing -- I've done the job of first trumpet. So he's saying -- bringing on these tunes, and we'll play tonight.

Now, we get on the stand. We'll play the opening. And I forget what the opening was. He's out there playing. went mad, People (unintelligible) brrrp, well, ray, ray, ray. He say play that tune I told you bring. Pull it out, we're going to do it. Play it, well, you know, I'm feeling -- I didn't have it. All the band pulled it out, but me. So I couldn't tell him -- say I haven't got it. I said okay. So I say there and closed my eyes, and when he brought his hand down I played the whole arrangements from memory.

Well, thank God I'm capable of doing that. I have what they call a photographic memory. I -- if I see a letter or an arrangement, or anything, I don't know, I seem to make a picture of it if I can remember where I saw
it. I have been like that for -- all my life, I guess.
It's a wonderful thing to have.

Yeah. So that helped me, so I closed my eyes. I was only worried about one spot that was in the second ending. You had the second ending going into -- key changes, where it goes from here to there to the other. Went through and it was beautiful, and I told him, and he siad What! Oh! He almost had a heart attack. He said whyn did you tell me? I said you -- I was, but you couldn't hear me.

But everything was all right. See? And I -- that I'm blessed. I was blessed with, and I'm glad, because even with this band, and Fats'band, and other bands I've been in, when I take a book, take the arrangements. I take them out, I remember them, and I play them, I fold them (unintelligible) and I very seldom, after that, open the book.
So from there on in it's just from memory?
From memory I play, and I memorize what I play, and if I feel like I'm getting a little stymied right quick, pssst, I turn to it. You know.
